I’m talking to you phrase

also hey, I’m talking to you, I’m speaking to you, are you listening?, I mean you

classical

Plaut. Men. 378: heus mulier, tibi dīcō
Ter. Eun. 336: Heus heus, tibi dīcō.

Tibi dīcō.

I’m talking to you; it’s you I mean

(vōx cōmica: Plaut., Ter.)

Said to someone who does not answer or will not stop, usually after heus.

Other words

  • Tibi ego dīcō. — it’s you I’m talking to

    also used · classical · Plaut. Curc. 516d: Heus tū, tibi ego dīcō.; Ter. And. 762: Tibi ego dīcō, annōn?

    (vōx cōmica: Plaut., Ter.)

Examples

  • Heus mulier, tibi dīcō. — Quid est?

    Hey, woman, I’m talking to you. — What is it?Plaut. Men. 378–378b

  • Heus tū, tibi dīcō, manē, redī.

    Hey you, I’m talking to you: wait, come back.Plaut. Men. 696–697

See also hey!, listen carefully, wait a moment!.

SourcesLewis & Short: dico

Plautus, Curculio 516d; Menaechmi 378–378b, 696–697. Terence, Andria 762; Eunuchus 336.
